title: Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services: Holds During Hospitalization, Discharge from Therapy and Plan Closing
content:
Rehabilitation department policy for **Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services** plans of care that pause, end or close.

## Clauses

> A plan is put on hold while the resident is hospitalized and resumes on return within the hold maximum days; past that, it is discharged as hold exceeded and a new evaluation is needed. The resident may decline further therapy at any time and the plan is then discharged as resident declined; a resident discharged from therapy is referred to the restorative nursing program at no charge. A discharged plan is closed only when its balance is zero.

The hold maximum is 30 days in every tier.

## Status changes

| From | To | When | What the record shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active | On hold | Treatment pauses while the resident is hospitalized | The first day on hold |
| On hold | Active | Treatment resumes after the resident returns within the hold limit | The hold start date is cleared |
| On hold | Discharged | The hold limit passes | The discharge date, with the reason hold exceeded |
| Active | Discharged | Goals are met, progress plateaus, the payer's authorization ends, or the resident declines further therapy | The discharge date, with the reason goals met, plateau, payer authorization ended or resident declined |
| Discharged | Closed | The resident charges for the plan are settled and the balance is zero | The closing date |

## Closing on a zero balance

A discharged plan is closed only when its balance is zero. This is judged on the system's record of the balance of that plan before it is closed.

| Hypothetical discharged plan | Closed? |
|---|---|
| Balance $0.00 | May be closed |
| Balance $8.43 still owed | Not closed |

## Hypothetical holds

- Hold started 4 May; the resident returns from hospital on 22 May, 18 days later: within the 30 days, so the plan resumes.
- Hold started 4 May; the resident is still away on 19 June, 46 days later: past the 30 days, so the plan is discharged as hold exceeded and a new evaluation is needed.

## Declining therapy and restorative nursing

The resident may decline further therapy at any time; the plan is then discharged as resident declined. A resident discharged from therapy is referred to the restorative nursing program at no charge.
